verses.1: But the LORD sent a large fish, that swallowed Jonah; and he remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
verses.2: From the belly of the fish Jonah said this prayer to the LORD, his God: "Set out for the great city of Nineveh, and announce to it the message that I will tell you."
verses.3: Out of my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me; From the midst of the nether world I cried for help, and you heard my voice. So Jonah made ready and went to Nineveh, according to the LORD'S bidding. Now Nineveh was an enormously large city; it took three days to go through it.
verses.4: For you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the sea, and the flood enveloped me; All your breakers and your billows passed over me. Jonah began his journey through the city, and had gone but a single day's walk announcing, "Forty days more and Nineveh shall be destroyed,"
verses.5: Then I said, "I am banished from your sight! yet would I again look upon your holy temple." when the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast and all of them, great and small, put on sackcloth.
verses.6: The waters swirled about me, threatening my life; the abyss enveloped me; seaweed clung about my head. When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in the ashes.
verses.7: Down I went to the roots of the mountains; the bars of the nether world were closing behind me forever, But you brought my life up from the pit, O LORD, my God. Then he had this proclaimed throughout Nineveh, by decree of the king and his nobles: "Neither man nor beast, neither cattle nor sheep, shall taste anything; they shall not eat, nor shall they drink water.
verses.8: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD; My prayer reached you in your holy temple. Man and beast shall be covered with sackcloth and call loudly to God; every man shall turn from his evil way and from the violence he has in hand.
verses.9: Those who worship vain idols forsake their source of mercy. Who knows, God may relent and forgive, and withhold his blazing wrath, so that we shall not perish."
verses.10: But I, with resounding praise, will sacrifice to you; What I have vowed I will pay: deliverance is from the LORD. When God saw by their actions how they turned from their evil way, he repented of the evil that he had threatened to do to them; he did not carry it out.
verses.11: Then the LORD commanded the fish to spew Jonah upon the shore. The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:

notes.text: Shall be destroyed: the Hebrew expression reminds the reader of the "overthrowing" of the wicked cities, Sodom and Gomorrah, by a special act of God.
Beast... sackcloth: the animals carried the signs of this repentance, as on occasions of joy they bore garlands.
